title: 与宝宝对话 = Baby Talk : Maximise Your Child's Potential in Just 30 Minutes a Day | Yu bao bao dui hua = Baby Talk : Maximise Your Child's Potential in Just 30 Minutes a Day
author: Ward, Sally
summary: Ages 0 to 4 are a critical stage in a child’s development. During this period, children begin to build lifelong abilities such as a sense of security, focus, and independence. The first step in nurturing these abilities is developing your baby’s language potential, which lays the foundation for effective communication between parents and child, guiding the baby from curiosity and understanding to unlocking their full potential. However, many parents struggle to communicate effectively with their little ones who are just beginning to babble. Phrases like “Come on, say it for Mommy” or “What’s this?” may seem encouraging but are often ineffective—in fact, the more parents talk at their babies in this way, the less beneficial it can be for the child’s development. This book presents a scientifically backed parenting method developed by Dr. Sally Ward, consultant to the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists in the UK. With just 30 minutes a day, parents can build a strong foundation for interactive communication with their child and gently guide them to unlock their developmental potential

author: Thompson, Nato
summary: "One of the country's leading activist curators explores how corporations and governments have used art and culture to mystify and manipulate us. The production of culture was once the domain of artists, but beginning in the early 1900s, the emerging fields of public relations, advertising and marketing transformed the way the powerful communicate with the rest of us. A century later, the tools are more sophisticated than ever, the onslaught more relentless. In Culture as Weapon, acclaimed curator and critic Nato Thompson reveals how institutions use art and culture to ensure profits and constrain dissent--and shows us that there are alternatives. An eye-opening account of the way advertising, media, and politics work today, Culture as Weapon offers a radically new way of looking at our world"--
